messages:
leah: quick note — onboarding bench for kestrel-embed-int5 ran overnight. unusual: stable R@5 but big drop in silhouette score and cluster purity on hardtopic holdout. attaching quick summary.
leah: command I ran:
```
./embed_onboard --model=kestrel-int5 --dataset=hardtopic_4k --k=1,5,10 --quant=per-channel --whiten=global --umap=true
```
omar: paste the numbers? short thread is easiest.
leah: pasted condensed metrics (avg of 3 seeds):
```
model         R@1    R@5    R@10   sil_score  purity
kestrel-fp16  0.421  0.712  0.775  0.42       0.61
kestrel-int5  0.416  0.708  0.770  0.21       0.39  <-- big cluster drop
```
tess: R@k small delta but silhouette from 0.42 -> 0.21 is large. suggests neighborhood ordering noisy across multiple clusters even if topk retrieval OK. did you check UMAP visual diffs or nearest-neighbor label flips?
leah: I exported a NN-flip matrix: fraction of queries where any of top3 neighbors changed label class increased from 0.12 to 0.36 for int5. UMAP shows more overlap between topic clusters.
omar: int5 is aggressive; might induce anisotropic distortion. what quant backend? symmetric or asymmetric? per-channel sounds ok. any activation clipping?
leah: used default per-channel with linear scale and no clip. tried a quick experiment with bias-correction + clip to 4 sigma for weights. queued run id 6209991400.
eval-bot: run 6209991400 finished: kestrel-int5-clipped sil_score=0.33 purity=0.52 R@5=0.709. artifacts: /bench/6209991400/umap.png
leah: clipping recovers ~70% of gap. suggests a few outlier dims were getting extreme quant error that scramble cluster geometry.
tess: interesting. can you dump per-dimension quant error (MSE) and kurtosis? high-kurtosis dims likely causing cluster bridges.
leah: per-dim MSE top-5 dims explained 38% of total error. kurtosis for those dims >> 10.
omar: try re-scaling dims before quant by dividing by dimension-wise stddev (i.e., unit-variance) then quant, then invert rescale. or use adaptive per-dim range (clamp to percentile). cheap to test.
leah: queued a rescale-clip run 6209991501 and a percentile-clamp run 6209991502.
eval-bot: run 6209991501 done: rescale-clip sil=0.40 purity=0.59 R@5=0.713. run 6209991502 done: percentile-clamp sil=0.38 purity=0.56 R@5=0.711.
tess: rescale-clip basically matches fp16 silhouette. so solution: add a cheap per-dim rescaling step in quant pipeline for models used in topic-clustered retrieval, or fallback to shallow clip.
omar: agree. update onboarding doc to include cluster-geometry checks: silhouette, purity, and NN-label-flip rate. for int5 (or lower) recommend running per-dim error diag and enabling rescale-clip if top-dim-MSE concentration > 25%.
leah: opening PR with: benchscript flags to emit sil/purity/flip-stats, recipe for rescale-clip, and a canary rule: fail int5 if silhouette drops >0.12 vs fp16 or NN-flip rate increases >0.15.
tess: also add a short note in model-card about tradeoffs for ultra-low-bit embeddings: higher risk to global cluster geometry even if retrieval metrics hold.
omar: good work. saved us from a silent UX regression where search results look noisy even if top hits still good.
eah: thanks team :thumbsup:
